tool.name: BAM read accounting
tool.description: idxstats, bam_stat counts and reads per region in one job
tool.command: ln -s '$input' input.bam && ln -s '$input.metadata.bam_index' input.bam.bai && samtools idxstats input.bam > '$idxstats' && samtools view input.bam | awk -v q='$mapq' -f '$bamstat_script' > '$bamstat' #if $regions && while IFS=\$'\t' read -r c s e n rest || [ -n "\$c" ]; do case "\$c" in ''|'#'*|track*|browser*) continue;; esac; printf '%s\t%s\t%s\t%s\t%s\n' "\$c" "\$s" "\$e" "\${n:-\$c:\$s-\$e}" "\$(samtools view -c -F 0x704 -q '$region_mapq' input.bam "\$c:\$((s + 1))-\$e")"; done < '$regions' > '$region_counts' #end if

configfiles.configfile:
# Counts of RSeQC bam_stat.py, in its output format, from samtools view text: every record is counted, # then QC-failed, duplicate, secondary and unmapped records are set aside in this order; the rest is # split at mapping quality q, and the records at or above it are counted by read, strand, splicing # (N in the CIGAR) and proper pairing (mate on another chromosome when RNEXT is neither = nor *). { total++ f = $2 + 0 if (and(f, 512)) { qc++; next } if (and(f, 1024)) { dup++; next } if (and(f, 256)) { nonprimary++; next } if (and(f, 4)) { unmapped++; next } if ($5 + 0 < q) { multi++; next } uniq++ if (and(f, 64)) read1++ if (and(f, 128)) read2++ if (and(f, 16)) reverse++ else forward++ if ($6 ~ /N/) splice++ else nonsplice++ if (and(f, 2)) { proper++ if ($7 != "=" && $7 != "*" && $7 != $3) diffchrom++ } } END { printf "
#==================================================
" printf "#All numbers are READ count
" printf "#==================================================

" printf "%-40s%d
", "Total records:", total printf "
" printf "%-40s%d
", "QC failed:", qc printf "%-40s%d
", "Optical/PCR duplicate:", dup printf "%-40s%d
", "Non primary hits", nonprimary printf "%-40s%d
", "Unmapped reads:", unmapped printf "%-40s%d
", "mapq < mapq_cut (non-unique):", multi printf "
" printf "%-40s%d
", "mapq >= mapq_cut (unique):", uniq printf "%-40s%d
", "Read-1:", read1 printf "%-40s%d
", "Read-2:", read2 printf "%-40s%d
", "Reads map to '+':", forward printf "%-40s%d
", "Reads map to '-':", reverse printf "%-40s%d
", "Non-splice reads:", nonsplice printf "%-40s%d
", "Splice reads:", splice printf "%-40s%d
", "Reads mapped in proper pairs:", proper printf "%-40s%d
", "Proper-paired reads map to different chrom:", diffchrom }

param.name: mapq
param.label: Minimum mapping quality for uniquely mapped reads
param.help: As -q of RSeQC bam_stat: records at or above it count as unique, below it as non-unique.

param.name: regions
param.label: Regions to count reads in
param.help: Optional BED (chrom, start, end, optional name), for example the span of the target gene. Counted are primary mapped reads that are not duplicates or QC-failed and overlap the region.

param.name: region_mapq
param.label: Minimum mapping quality for the region counts

tool.help:
**What it does**
Reads a BAM once for the read accounting that otherwise needs two tools:
- **idxstats**: the output of ``samtools idxstats`` (per reference: length, mapped, unmapped). - **bam_stat**: the counts and the text format of **RSeQC bam_stat.py**: total records, QC failed, duplicates, non-primary hits, unmapped, below and at or above the mapping quality cut, and for the uniquely mapped records read 1 and 2, strand, splicing, proper pairs and proper pairs with the mate on another chromosome. Byte-identical to bam_stat.py with the same ``-q``. - **reads per region** (optional): for every BED region, the primary mapped reads overlapping it (no duplicates, no QC-failed reads), for example in the span of the target gene.
Because both outputs match the original tools exactly, steps that read them stay unchanged.
